register.text: Strengthens the power grid and helps businesses use energy more efficiently, for a clean transition that shields the economy from global energy volatility. It serves the energy standard and the livelihoods of industrial enterprises.

register.note: Brings the total project investment to $34.5 million

register.name: Basic Education Improvement Project
register.detail: IDA credit · Approved, release of 29 August 2025 · $5 million Early Learning Partnership grant
register.text: Finances over 900 new classrooms, mentoring and coaching for more than 37,000 teachers, 60 public childcare centres and 60 new preschool classes. Over 1.7 million children are set to benefit from improved primary schooling, which serves education, the standard furthest from reach in Cambodia.
register.note: Plus a $5 million Early Learning Partnership grant

register.text: Irrigation and water security for farmers.

register.name: Second Growth and Resilience DPF
register.text: Budget support for growth and resilience.

register.name: Water Supply and Sanitation Acceleration Project
register.text: Piped water and sanitation for towns and cities.

register.name: Smallholder Resilient Economic Development Sector Project
register.detail: Release of 26 October 2026 · $57 million concessional loan and $15 million grant from the Asian Development Fund · Cofinancing: ASEAN Infrastructure Fund $23 million, Green Climate Fund $10 million grant, Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific $3 million grant
register.text: Upgrades irrigation for 7,000 more hectares, rehabilitates 190 kilometres of access roads and trains farmers in resilient crop, horticulture, poultry, insect and aquaculture practices across 186 communes, with grants to reduce reliance on imported fuel and fertilisers. register.note: About 200,000 smallholder farmers in seven provinces

register.name: RISE Program: AIIB cofinancing
register.detail: Approved 4 September 2026 · Sovereign · Policy-based cofinancing, ADB the lead cofinancier · Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility · Ministry of Economy and Finance
register.text: Policy-based cofinancing to help Cambodia mitigate the adverse economic and social impacts of the Middle East situation, alongside the Asian Development Bank and JICA. It serves the energy, food and livelihood standards.
register.note: Cofinances ADB’s Rapid Intervention for Stabilization of the Economy Program

register.name: Rapid Intervention for Stabilization of the Economy (RISE) Program
register.detail: Approved by the ADB Board 30 July 2026 · Ordinary capital resources, concessional · 24 years with 8 years’ grace · 1.0% a year in the grace period, 1.5% thereafter
register.text: Supports temporary, targeted fiscal measures, protects planned social spending in the 2026 budget and backs clean energy technologies. It funds income support for more than one million poor households registered under IDPoor, at least 350,000 of them headed by women, and debt relief and farm inputs in rural areas, which serves the food, energy and livelihood standards.
register.note: Combined financing with AIIB and JICA could reach $688 million

register.name: Utility-Scale Battery Energy Storage Project
register.detail: Approved, release of 24 June 2026 · $40 million concessional loan and $5 million grant from the Asian Development Fund · $18.44 million from the Green Climate Fund and the United Kingdom through the ASEAN Catalytic Green Finance Facility · 250 MW / 500 MWh
register.text: A 250 MW, 500 MWh battery storage system that stores surplus renewable power and dispatches it to the grid to manage peak loads and stabilise fluctuations, and strengthens the capacity of Electricité du Cambodge. It serves the energy standard and Cambodia’s target of 70% renewable energy capacity by 2030.
register.note: At the Takeo substation, southern Cambodia

register.name: Emergency Support Loan for Enhancing Economic Resilience and Stable Energy Supply
register.detail: Signed 28 October 2026, Phnom Penh · Up to ¥30 billion · 2.8% · 25 years with 7 years’ grace · General untied · Ministry of Economy and Finance
register.text: Budget support for economic stabilisation and energy transition measures, to strengthen supply chain resilience and ease the effects of high energy and raw material prices and supply disruptions linked to the Middle East situation. It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.detail: Signed 11 August 2026, Phnom Penh · Up to ¥17,776 million · TORF+45bp; consulting 1.10% · 30 years with 10 years’ grace · Port Authority of Sihanoukville
register.text: A new container terminal, dredging of sailing routes and berths, a customs inspection yard and cargo-handling equipment, including quay and rubber-tired gantry cranes. JICA expects it to improve the logistics environment, which serves the livelihood standard.
register.note: At Cambodia’s only international deep-sea port

register.name: Southwest Phnom Penh Irrigation and Drainage Rehabilitation and Improvement Project (III)
register.detail: Signed 25 June 2026, Phnom Penh · ¥24,237 million · TORF+35bp; consulting 0.80% · 25 years with 7 years’ grace · Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology
register.text: Rehabilitates irrigation and drainage facilities southwest of Phnom Penh, with irrigation associations and farming guidance, to improve farm productivity and reduce flood damage, including in the wider capital. It serves the food and livelihood standards.
register.note: Kampong Speu, Takeo and Kandal provinces

register.name: Flood Protection and Drainage Improvement Project in Phnom Penh Capital City (I)
register.detail: Signed 30 April 2026, Phnom Penh · Up to ¥6,908 million · TORF+25bp; consulting 0.8% · 25 years with 7 years’ grace · Phnom Penh Capital Administration
register.text: A new box culvert, a rehabilitated open channel, a retention basin and a drainage pumping station, to enhance stormwater drainage capacity and mitigate flood damage in the capital. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: SchneiTec Jupiter green infrastructure project bond
register.detail: Listed on the Cambodia Securities Exchange, release of 16 November 2026 · S&P Global Ratings “Dark Green” assessment · Part of a $150 million financing package
register.text: A bond of a Cambodian-owned special purpose company, which the Global Green Growth Institute calls a record green infrastructure bond on the exchange. It anchors a $150 million package for a 350 MW solar plant, part of the 930 MW Chheu Tom Solar Complex, expected to power more than 200,000 Cambodian households, which serves the energy standard.
register.note: 350 MW of solar in Krakor district, Pursat province

register.text: Long-term debt for a greenfield 150 MW solar plant with a 30 MW battery storage system and a 22 kV line to a nearby substation, sponsored by SchneiTec Company Ltd. It serves the energy standard.
register.note: DEG’s part of senior debt of up to $127 million

dispatches.label: 16 Nov 2026
dispatches.author: steward
dispatches.title: SchneiTec Jupiter lists a record US$99 million green bond in Cambodia
dispatches.summary: On 16 November 2026 SchneiTec Jupiter listed a US$99 million green infrastructure project bond on the Cambodia Securities Exchange, a record for the exchange, anchoring a US$150 million package for a 350 MW solar plant in Pursat province.
body: On 16 November 2026 the Global Green Growth Institute reported that SchneiTec Jupiter, a Cambodian-owned special purpose company, had listed a US$99 million infrastructure project bond on the Cambodia Securities Exchange. The Institute describes it as a record green infrastructure bond for the exchange.

The bond is structured to align with the ICMA Green Bond Principles and the ASEAN Green Bond Standards, and S&P Global Ratings assigned it a “Dark Green” assessment under its Shades of Green method. The release does not state the tenor, the coupon or the arrangers.

The bond anchors a US$150 million financing package for a 350 MW solar photovoltaic plant in Krakor district, Pursat province, which is expected to power more than 200,000 Cambodian households. The plant is part of the 930 MW Chheu Tom Solar Complex. The release does not break down the rest of the package.

It moves energy, one of the seven standards: new generating capacity paid for through the nation’s own capital market rather than a sovereign loan. A sister company, SchneiTec Dynamic, listed a US$50 million bond on the exchange last year with technical assistance from the Cambodia Sustainable Bond Accelerator, which the Institute runs with funding from Luxembourg.

The model could work for Laos: a project company issues a certified green bond on its national exchange to finance a single solar plant, and a technical-assistance facility helps a young market list its first large green issues.
